title: Rollout interlock contract & slice orchestration notes (draft)
content:
Purpose
---
Working notes for defining the cross-functional 'interlock contract' that must be satisfied before progressive exposure of model/behavior changes. Focus is on slice orchestration (how we pick cohorts), required signoffs, and clear gating signals for canary + A/B experiments that affect latency/cost/quality. This is intentionally pragmatic — aim: reduce back-and-forth during launches and give SRE/QA/CS a concise checklist they can run against.

Context and scope
---
- Applies to: any change that (a) alters model or routing logic, (b) changes inference runtime config (batching/quant), or (c) modifies cost-sensitive routing policies.
- Excludes: purely UI copy changes or analytics-only pipelines.
- Teams involved: Product (feature owner), Serving Runtime, SRE, Observability, QA/Applied ML, Solutions/Customer Success for externally visible experiments.

Interlock contract (summary)
---
Minimal set of preconditions (all must be green before exposing to user traffic beyond dev/staging):
1) Smoke pass on staging with production-like traffic replay (>= 10k requests or 24h of synthetic mix).
2) Latency baseline delta defined and acceptable (p50/p95/p99 buckets) + cost delta estimate approved by product finance.
3) Canary cohort plan: explicit slices (IDs) + allocation schedule + rollback thresholds per slice.
4) Observability: dashboards, alerts, trace sampling knobs, and a tagged dashboard cell for the experiment id.
5) Rollback plan: automatic revert triggers (SRE) + manual rollback path (product + oncall).
6) Customer impact signoff: CS + legal if experiment touches customer-visible model outputs or can be served to paid customers.

Signoff owners (who signs what)
---
- Product owner: validates experiment goal, hypothesis, traffic plan, and UX communications.
- Applied ML / QA: verifies prompt set/regression tests, evaluation harness run, and scoring thresholds.
- SRE / Serving Runtime: validates autoscaling behaviour, fallback variant exists, and rollback automation.
- Observability: dashboard created, SLOs instrumented, and alert runbook linked.
- Finance (for Dedicated/DPO customers): verifies cost delta and approves burn rate.
- Solutions/CS: approves customer-facing comms and checks for high-risk customers.

Slice selection heuristics (practical)
---
- Start small. Default slices should map to orthogonal dimensions: geography, platform, traffic tier (free/premium), device family, and API call shape.
- Prefer deterministic hashing on user_id or tenant_id to maintain consistent membership across waves.
- Avoid slices that correlate strongly with sensitive attributes unless the experiment specifically targets them.
- Example initial sequence (for a latency-risk feature): 0.1% global -> 1% regional (low risk region) -> 5% cross-section -> 20% internal customers -> 50% if stable.

Traffic shaping and A/B allocation patterns
---
- For feature-flags/canaries: use exponentially increasing allocations and hold windows (e.g., 1h, 6h, 24h) depending on risk.
- For A/B tests measuring engagement or quality: prefer steady-state allocation with a minimum statistical power calculation. Record expected effect size and min sample size in experiment doc.
- Use adaptive buffering: when CPU/GPU p95 crosses threshold, throttle experimental slice automatically and route to baseline variant.

Observability & metrics (required set)
---
Primary signals (real-time):
- Latency (p50/p95/p99) per-slice, per-model variant.
- Token throughput and GPU utilization for serving clusters used by the experiment.
- Error rates: model errors, infra errors, 5xx/timeout rates.
- Quality regressions: eval harness score delta on canary prompt set.
- Cost signals: estimated $/k tokens per model variant.

Secondary signals (near-real time / daily):
- User-facing metrics (CTR, completion rates, retention if relevant).
- Human QA flags and customer reports.
- Drift in input distribution (prompt length, tokens, special tokens).

Alerting thresholds (examples)
---
- Critical: p99 latency > baseline_p99 + 400ms for >5 minutes OR error rate > baseline_error + 0.5% over 5 minutes -> auto-revert + page SRE.
- High: p95 latency increase > 150ms sustained for 15 minutes -> notif to oncall + pause progression.
- Quality: eval score drop > X% (model-specific threshold) on canary prompt set -> stop rollout for triage.
- Cost: $/k tokens increase > 25% over baseline -> require finance signoff for further rollout.

Rollback matrix and decision tree
---
- Auto triggers (SRE-controlled): infra errors, autoscaler thrash, severe latency breaches as above.
- Manual rollback: product or QA escalates if user-visible regressions occur. Follow: pause traffic -> shift slice to baseline -> validate -> full revert if persistent.
- Post-rollback: incident blameless postmortem and retained experiment artifacts for 90 days.

Canary automation checklist (preflight)
---
- [ ] Canary config created in feature-flag service with experiment_id tag.
- [ ] Deterministic hashing key set and verified on test requests.
- [ ] Rollout plan annotated with hold windows and escalation contacts.
- [ ] Dashboards: time-series with slice/v variant filter. Update SLO docs with experiment link.
- [ ] Alert policies bound to experiment tag.
- [ ] Fallback routes available and smoke-tested (switch 1% traffic to fallback).

A/B experiment design addenda
---
- Register hypothesis, target metrics, expected direction and minimal detectable effect in experiment tracking sheet.
- Add blocking criteria: sample size not met or contaminated traffic (spam/bots).
- For longer-lived experiments (>2 weeks), schedule once-per-day sanity checks and automated half-time analysis for drift.

Risk notes / edge cases (random thoughts)
---
- Multi-variant experiments that touch routing decisions can create combinatorial blowups; prefer sequential experiments or hierarchical gating.
- Cached prefix behavior: if a canary warms KV cache then reverts, baseline traffic might see warmed caches — design cold-start windows in hold schedule.
- Offline eval vs. online feedback can diverge; always require a small live canary even if offline looks perfect.
- For Dedicated customers, ensure private routing rules are not violated by global experiments. Tag tenants and exclude by default unless opt-in.

Communication plan
---
- Pre-launch: 24h notice to SRE+Observability+CS with experiment doc link + expected timeline.
- Live: experiment status updates in #prod-rollouts every hold-window boundary.
- Post: summary in product release notes + decision (promote/rollback) and small postmortem if any threshold breached.

Open questions / TODOs
---
- [ ] Formalize cost-obligation matrix for experiments that exceed X% of baseline monthly spend (who bears delta?).
- [ ] Define standard stat test library and default MDE values for common metrics (latency, quality).
- [ ] Add automated experiment tagging to traces for easier debugging (trace-id -> experiment id). Evan to prototype.

Appendix: quick start template (to copy into new experiment doc)
---
- Title:
- Owner:
- Hypothesis:
- Key metrics + baseline values:
- Experiment id (ff-service):
- Initial slice ids + allocation schedule:
- Hold windows (hrs):
- Rollback triggers (explicit):
- Dashboards & runbook links:
- Signoffs obtained (list names):

Notes to self: keep the template minimal — the goal is to reduce friction for small risky launches and ensure heavyweight launches still get the scrutiny they need. This doc should evolve into a checklist that maps to the Console's rollout UI and the feature flag service.
